messages:
Alex K: ran the 1h perf sweep on the prefills vs decode separation idea. Results look promising but noisy. 95th latency down ~12% for long-prefill tails, but small-gen p50 regressed ~4%. attaching quick notes.
Maria P: can you paste the flame/sample logs? curious if kernel churn caused the p50 hit.
Alex K: paste of a small extract below — prefill split caused more consistent kernel selection for large-seqs, but apparently increased short-decoder scheduling contention.
```
# prefill-run summary
prefill-batch-size-target=48
decode-batch-size-target=8
token-budget-prefill=300
token-budget-decode=40
kernel-selection: prefer-fp16-matmul-v2 for prefill
```
Jiwon L: fyi the profiler shows frequent kernel rebinds when we mix small-decode requests onto the same worker that just executed a large prefill kernel. KV cache warmups look fine though.
Samir R: noticed KV cache thrash: when prefill-heavy traffic lands, we hit cold entries then decode requests suffer higher lookup latency. Might be because the prefill path evicts small-keysets used by chat sessions.
Lisa T: any chance the p50 regression is from token-bucket enforcement delay? we added an extra soft-wait when switching phase.
Alex K: yeah that was my suspicion. The scheduler currently does a soft-yield on phase change: sleep 1-2ms to flush window. For short decodes that overhead dominates.
Maria P: can we do phase-aware fast-path: if decode token_budget < 32 and queue_len < 4, bypass soft-yield and allow decode worker to run immediately? sounds safe.
Jiwon L: i tested that heuristic locally — reduces p50 regression to ~1% and keeps 95th improvements. patch attached.
```
diff --git a/scheduler.cpp b/scheduler.cpp
index 12345..67890 100644
--- a/scheduler.cpp
+++ b/scheduler.cpp
@@ -412,6 +412,13 @@ bool Scheduler::should_yield_for_phase_change(Request &r) {
-  if (r.phase != worker.phase) return true;
+  if (r.phase != worker.phase) {
+    if (r.phase == PHASE_DECODE && r.token_budget < 32 && r.queue_len < 4) return false;
+    return true;
+  }
+  return false;
 }
```
Samir R: looks reasonable. also propose adding a lightweight KV-hit score to prefer placing decode work on workers with recent KV hits for that session id.
Alex K: agreed — KV affinity could help. simplest start: if session_id has recent_kv_hits > 0, prefer same worker for next decode. fallback stays the same.
Maria P: what about kernel selection side-effects? if we keep affinity, we might pin small decodes to fp16 kernels that are suboptimal for weird sequence lengths.
Jiwon L: true — add a quick re-eval step: when picking kernel do quick-cost-estimate(cost_fp16, cost_int8) and prefer lower expected tail latency. cost_estimate uses cached seq_histogram per-session.
Lisa T: also want to instrument a per-route metric: prefills_per_minute, decode_queue_wait_ms, kv_hit_rate. without those we can't correlate.
deploy-bot: benchmark run queued: job/infra/1898765432-prefill-split-try1 — results posted to /tmp/bench-1898765432.log when done.
Alex K: next actions:
- merge heuristic bypass for small decode token_budget (<32)
- add KV-affinity opt-in flag + metric
- kernel quick-cost-estimate hook
- run 3x canary with traffic mix (90% chat short, 10% long-prefill)
I'll push a draft PR in a bit. comments welcome. :slightly_smiling_face:
Maria P: cheers, thanks for the writeup. if canary is green, we should document the new token_budget knobs and default them conservatively.
Jiwon L: i'll add profiler dashboards and a sample trace template for investigating kernel rebinds.
Samir R: i'll prototype KV-affinity in a branch and add unit tests simulating eviction patterns.
Lisa T: i'll add the metrics to console and a quick alert for decode_queue_wait_ms > 20ms sustained.
Alex K: perfect. meeting-free sync here; ping me if you hit blockers."
